newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Tuesday in quiet trading as the market awaited the central bank's announcement on interest rates next Monday, traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.16 pct to 111.73
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.2 pct to 112.08
* Unlinked government bonds: +0.07 pct to 110.87
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.1 pct at 110.84
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct to 108.95
Volume including Makams was a low 135 million shekels.
"Unlinked bonds traded steady today while CPI-linked bonds continued their positive trend," said Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House.
Prices of both unlinked and CPI-linked bonds had risen after the publication of July's consumer price index (CPI) on Friday.
The July index rose by 1.0 percent, at the low end of economists' expectations of 1.0 to 1.2 percent. In June the CPI rose by 1.1 percent.
"The central bank today issued 900 million shekels worth of Makams, which closed at yields higher than market yields. This indicates there were not that many buyers," Weisberg said.
He said short Makams closed at 13.5 percent and long Makams at 13.4 percent against market yields averaging 13.2 percent.
"We may see prices of unlinked bonds close lower tomorrow as a correction to the price rises we saw in the last few days since publication of the CPI," Weisberg said.
He said prices of CPI-linked bonds were likely to edge higher until the central bank publishes its key lending rate for September on Monday.
"The market expects the central bank to raise interest rates by 0.3 to 0.5 percentage point," said Eyal Segal of United Mizrahi Bank.
The base rate has been 12.7 percent since the middle of June.
Weisberg said that despite the expected rate hike, the feeling was that in the longer term interest rates would stabilise or decline.
"Until publication of the next CPI, unlinked bonds are expected to remain stable while yields of CPI-linked bonds are likely to fall lower," Weisberg said.
Prices of dollar-linked bonds rose on Tuesday on the strengthening of the dollar against the shekel.
The shekel weakened against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies on Tuesday following the rise of the U.S. currency on overseas markets, dealers said.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5320 shekels compared with 3.5220 on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.53 shekels)
